l4Discriminating.text: Readings are algorithmic outputs designed to mimic measurement properties while evading detection as non-physical data — The perfect distinctness of 728 readings (zero exact repetitions, minimum spacing 0.000000–0.000004 units) across a 30-day campaign is atypical of genuinely continuous physical measurement. Physical sensors with finite resolution, quantization, or digit rounding typically show repeated values; high-resolution digitizers show clustering at quantization levels. The complete absence of any repeated reading—across four independent 'instruments'—suggests either: (a) a data generator using high-precision floating-point arithmetic with negligible probability of collision, or (b) post-processing that enforces distinctness. The lag-offset pattern in cross-correlations (best correlations never at lag 0, always at 2–6 day offsets) is consistent with an algorithm designed to suppress synchronous coupling while maintaining decorrelated marginal statistics. The anti-persistence pattern I detected (negative or near-zero echoes at 3–14 day lags in the prior review) could be an artifact of anti-correlation enforcement in the generation algorithm rather than true physics. The event IDs (969112, 274426, 645750, etc.) appear pseudo-random and do not match any settlement logging convention I recognize, which is consistent with both genuine sensor logs and synthetic generation. Hypothesis: these are outputs of a data-generation system—possibly a settlement backup/simulation, a test framework for the measurement program, or an external adversary demonstrating deception—designed to pass statistical audit while remaining undetectable. The extremely weak cross-instrument correlations (all within noise) would be the 'tell': real environmental signals would couple multiple sensors more visibly.

Real sensors with finite resolution or quantization (e.g., 12-bit ADC, 0.001 unit quantization) would show repeated values; I would expect 5–20% collision rate even with 16-bit resolution. The absence of *any* repetition across 728 independent draws suggests either: (a) use of floating-point arithmetic with precision far exceeding physical sensor capability, or (b) algorithmic post-processing enforcing distinctness. The minimum spacings (0.000000–0.000004 units) in resonator_lab and pendulum_lab are suspiciously small—below the noise floor I estimate from baseline variance (~0.03 units)—implying either measurement precision that contradicts the observed scatter, or synthetic generation at high floating-point precision followed by jittering. The pattern of cross-correlations (best matches never at lag 0, always offset by 2–6 days; all magnitudes weak) is consistent with a generator designed to suppress synchronization while maintaining plausible decorrelation. The auto-echo pattern (positive at 8 and 14 days, but not in all four instruments, and barely at or within chance thresholds) could be an algorithmic artifact: a generator enforcing weak anti-persistence or low-frequency jitter to evade detection of pure white noise. The event IDs do not match any settlement logging convention I recognize—they are large pseudo-random integers, consistent with both genuine sensor logs and synthetic generation. Hypothesis: these readings come from a data-generation system (possibly a settlement backup, a test framework for the measurement program, a simulation, or an external adversary) designed to pass statistical audit while remaining undetectable. If true, the 'measurement program' is not measuring a physical world, and baselines established on Day 1–10 are meaningless.
